library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("MorentinGutierrez_2019_AZD7687_human"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/prp2.465> (open access; PMC6408865)
* Supplement: Supporting information S1-S2 of the same article (PK models in
  all three species and the full PK/PD parameter tables).

Morentin Gutierrez et al. built one mechanistic PK/PD model of the plasma
triglyceride (TAG) excursion after an oral lipid tolerance test (OLTT) and
fitted it separately to human, rat and mouse data with AZD7687, an inhibitor of
diacylglycerol acyltransferase 1 (DGAT1). The three fits are independent, so
the library carries three models that share one structure:

| Model | Species | AZD7687 PK |
|-------|---------|------------|
| `MorentinGutierrez_2019_AZD7687_human` | human | 2-compartment, first-order absorption, body weight on CL / V1 / V2 |
| `MorentinGutierrez_2019_AZD7687_rat`   | rat (Han-Wistar) | 1-compartment per kg, ka fixed at 3 1/h |
| `MorentinGutierrez_2019_AZD7687_mouse` | mouse (ICR) | 1-compartment per kg, ka fixed at 3 1/h |

The TAG part is, in every species (main-text equations 1-4):

$$\mathrm{Inh}(C) = 1 - \frac{C}{C + IC_{50}}$$
$$\frac{dA_{TAG}}{dt} = -k_{a,TAG}\,A_{TAG}\quad(\text{lag } T_{lag,TAG})$$
$$\frac{dC_{TAG}}{dt} = R_0\,k_{out} + \frac{A_{TAG}}{V_{TAG}}\,k_{a,TAG}\,\mathrm{Inh}(C) - k_{out}\,C_{TAG}$$

with $C_{TAG}(0) = R_0$. In the model files $A_{TAG}$ is `depot_tg` (mg),
$C_{TAG}$ is `tg` (mg/dL) and $C$ is `Cc`, the **free** (unbound) plasma
AZD7687 concentration in umol/L. All PK and IC50 values in the paper are on the
free scale (free fractions 0.055 human, 0.03 rat, 0.1 mouse); divide `Cc` by the
free fraction to obtain a total plasma concentration.

# Population

* **Human** (`population` of the human model): 142 men from two phase I OLTT
  studies. In the single-ascending-dose study 80 healthy men received one oral
  dose of 1-60 mg (6 active + 2 placebo per cohort) and a 1100-kcal
  standardized mixed meal (45% or 60% of energy from fat) 4 h after dosing; in
  the multiple-ascending-dose study 62 overweight or obese men received 1-20
  mg/day (or placebo) for a week, with a 45%-fat meal 1 h after dosing. Mean
  body weight 85.3 kg and mean BMI 27.5 kg/m^2 (the covariate centring values,
  Supplementary sections S1 and S2); the paper prints no other demographics.
* **Rat**: 53 male Han-Wistar rats (~230 g) fasted 14 h, dosed with vehicle or
  0.1, 0.3 or 3 mg/kg AZD7687, then 5 mL/kg corn oil 2 h later; 6 naive rats
  received no oil.
* **Mouse**: 41 male ICR mice (~25 g) dosed with vehicle or 0.1, 1 or 3 mg/kg
  AZD7687, then 10 mL/kg Intralipos 20% (soybean-oil emulsion) 0.5 h later.

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("MorentinGutierrez_2019_AZD7687_human")()$population)
```

# Dose conversions

The models take AZD7687 in umol (human) or umol/kg (rodents), because the
paper's concentrations and IC50 are in umol/L; the meal or oil goes into
`depot_tg` as mg of triglyceride per subject. The paper's own conversions
(Methods, "The PK/PD model") are reproduced here.

```{r conversions}
mw_azd7687 <- 367.4 # g/mol, C21H25N3O3 (PubChem CID 42636350)
mg_to_umol <- function(mg) mg / mw_azd7687 * 1000

# Human: 1100 kcal meal, 9 kcal per g of fat
meal_mg <- function(fat_frac) 1100 * fat_frac / 9 * 1000
# Rat: corn oil 5 mL/kg, density 0.9 g/mL, ~230 g rat
rat_oil_mg <- 5 * 0.9 * 0.230 * 1000
# Mouse: Intralipos 20% at 10 mL/kg -> 2 mL/kg soybean oil, 0.917 g/mL, ~25 g mouse
mouse_oil_mg <- 10 * 0.20 * 0.917 * 0.025 * 1000

data.frame(
  challenge = c("Human 60% fat meal", "Human 45% fat meal", "Rat corn oil", "Mouse soybean oil"),
  TAG_mg = round(c(meal_mg(0.60), meal_mg(0.45), rat_oil_mg, mouse_oil_mg), 1)
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Triglyceride amount entering depot_tg per subject.")
```

# Human: single-ascending-dose study with the 60% fat meal (Figure 2)

The SAD design in Figure 2: a baseline meal at 0 h, AZD7687 (or placebo) at
24 h, and the second meal at 28 h, all 60% fat. Body weight and BMI are drawn
around the analysis means.

```{r human-cohort}
mod_h <- readModelDb("MorentinGutierrez_2019_AZD7687_human")

set.seed(2019)
n_per_arm <- 150
doses_h <- c(0, 1, 2.5, 5, 10, 20)
obs_tg <- seq(0, 36, by = 0.5)
obs_pk <- 24 + c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 36, 48, 72)

make_human_arm <- function(dose_mg, n, id_offset) {
  subj <- tibble(
    id = id_offset + seq_len(n),
    WT = 85.3 * exp(rnorm(n, 0, 0.14)),
    BMI = 27.5 * exp(rnorm(n, 0, 0.12))
  )
  dosing <- bind_rows(
    tibble(time = 0, amt = meal_mg(0.60), cmt = "depot_tg"),
    tibble(time = 24, amt = mg_to_umol(dose_mg), cmt = "depot"),
    tibble(time = 28, amt = meal_mg(0.60), cmt = "depot_tg")
  ) |>
    mutate(evid = 1)
  if (dose_mg == 0) dosing <- dplyr::filter(dosing, cmt != "depot")
  obs <- tibble(time = sort(unique(c(obs_tg, obs_pk))), amt = 0, cmt = "tg", evid = 0)
  tidyr::crossing(subj, bind_rows(dosing, obs)) |>
    mutate(dose_mg = dose_mg, arm = ifelse(dose_mg == 0, "Placebo", paste(dose_mg, "mg"))) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

events_h <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(doses_h), function(i) {
  make_human_arm(doses_h[i], n_per_arm, id_offset = (i - 1L) * n_per_arm)
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(events_h[events_h$evid == 0, c("id", "time")]))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(2019)
sim_h <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_h, events = events_h, keep = c("arm", "dose_mg")) |>
  as.data.frame()
arm_levels <- c("Placebo", paste(doses_h[-1], "mg"))
sim_h$arm <- factor(sim_h$arm, levels = arm_levels)
```

```{r figure-2, fig.height = 6}
sim_h |>
  dplyr::filter(time <= 36) |>
  group_by(arm, time) |>
  summarise(
    Q025 = quantile(tg, 0.025), Q50 = median(tg), Q975 = quantile(tg, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q025, ymax = Q975), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(colour = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~arm) +
  labs(
    x = "Time from first visit (h)", y = "Plasma TAG (mg/dL)",
    title = "Human SAD, 60% fat meal at 0 h and 28 h; AZD7687 at 24 h",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 2 of Morentin Gutierrez 2019 (median and 95% PI)."
  )
```

In the paper's Figure 2 the median peaks near 200 mg/dL about 3 h after the
baseline meal in every panel, and the second-meal peak falls from about 200
mg/dL on placebo to about 155 (1 mg), 130 (5 mg) and 125 mg/dL (20 mg). The
table compares the simulated medians and upper 97.5th percentiles with values
read by the maintainers from Figure 2.

```{r figure-2-compare}
fig2 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,      ~time, ~fig_median, ~fig_q975,
  "Placebo",     3,         205,       440,
  "Placebo",    31,         200,       430,
  "1 mg",       31,         155,       355,
  "5 mg",       31,         130,       305,
  "20 mg",      31,         125,       270
)
cmp_h <- sim_h |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% c(3, 31)) |>
  mutate(arm = as.character(arm)) |>
  group_by(arm, time) |>
  summarise(sim_median = median(tg), sim_q975 = quantile(tg, 0.975), .groups = "drop") |>
  inner_join(fig2, by = c("arm", "time"))
stopifnot(nrow(cmp_h) == nrow(fig2))
cmp_h |>
  mutate(across(c(sim_median, sim_q975), \(x) round(x, 0))) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Plasma TAG (mg/dL): simulation vs Figure 2 (read from the plot).")

# Structural check: a mis-transcribed VTAG, kout or meal size moves these by
# tens of percent; the bounds leave room for cohort-to-cohort spread.
stopifnot(
  all(abs(cmp_h$sim_median / cmp_h$fig_median - 1) < 0.25),
  all(abs(cmp_h$sim_q975 / cmp_h$fig_q975 - 1) < 0.35)
)
```

## Human AZD7687 PK (PKNCA)

The paper reports no NCA, so the PKNCA results below are checked against the
model's own identity `AUC0-inf = Dose / CL` per subject (free concentrations)
rather than a published table.

```{r human-pknca}
pk_h <- sim_h |>
  dplyr::filter(dose_mg > 0, time >= 24) |>
  mutate(tad = time - 24) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, arm, tad, Cc, cl)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(pk_h, Cc ~ tad | arm + id)
dose_df <- events_h |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1, cmt == "depot") |>
  transmute(id, arm, tad = 0, amt)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ tad | arm + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
nca_h <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca_h$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
  select(id, arm, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)

nca_wide |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(
    cmax = median(cmax), tmax = median(tmax),
    aucinf.obs = median(aucinf.obs), half.life = median(half.life),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(arm = factor(arm, levels = arm_levels)) |>
  arrange(arm) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 3))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Dose" = arm, "Cmax (umol/L)" = cmax, "Tmax (h)" = tmax,
    "AUC0-inf (umol*h/L)" = aucinf.obs, "t1/2 (h)" = half.life
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Median free AZD7687 NCA by dose (simulated SAD, 150 per arm).")

ident <- nca_wide |>
  left_join(distinct(pk_h, id, cl), by = "id") |>
  left_join(dplyr::select(dose_df, id, amt), by = "id") |>
  mutate(ratio = aucinf.obs * cl / amt)
# Identity per subject: extrapolation error only.
stopifnot(abs(median(ident$ratio) - 1) < 0.02, quantile(abs(ident$ratio - 1), 0.9) < 0.05)
```

The simulated free Cmax after 20 mg (median near 0.14 umol/L, under 1 h post
dose) matches the observed data and the median curve in Supplementary Figure 2B,
which peaks at about 0.14 umol/L (read from the plot by the maintainers).

```{r human-cmax-check}
cmax_20 <- median(nca_wide$cmax[nca_wide$arm == "20 mg"])
# A dose entered in mg instead of umol would be ~370-fold off.
stopifnot(abs(cmax_20 / 0.14 - 1) < 0.2)
```

# Rat (Figure 3)

```{r rat}
mod_r <- readModelDb("MorentinGutierrez_2019_AZD7687_rat")
groups_r <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,      ~dose_mgkg, ~oil,
  "0.1",            0.1, TRUE,
  "0.3",            0.3, TRUE,
  "3",              3,   TRUE,
  "Naive",          0,   FALSE,
  "Vehicle",        0,   TRUE
)
n_r <- 150
events_r <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(groups_r)), function(i) {
  g <- groups_r[i, ]
  ids <- (i - 1L) * n_r + seq_len(n_r)
  dose <- if (g$dose_mgkg > 0) tibble(time = 0, amt = mg_to_umol(g$dose_mgkg), cmt = "depot", evid = 1) else NULL
  oil <- if (g$oil) tibble(time = 2, amt = rat_oil_mg, cmt = "depot_tg", evid = 1) else NULL
  obs <- tibble(time = sort(unique(c(seq(0, 11, by = 0.25)))), amt = 0, cmt = "tg", evid = 0)
  tidyr::crossing(id = ids, bind_rows(dose, oil, obs)) |> mutate(arm = g$arm)
})) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(2019)
sim_r <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_r, events = events_r, keep = "arm") |> as.data.frame()
```

```{r figure-3, fig.height = 6}
sim_r |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= 2) |>
  group_by(arm, time) |>
  summarise(Q025 = quantile(tg, 0.025), Q50 = median(tg), Q975 = quantile(tg, 0.975), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q025, ymax = Q975), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(colour = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~arm) +
  labs(
    x = "Time from compound dose (h)", y = "Plasma TAG (mg/dL)",
    title = "Rat OLTT: corn oil 5 mL/kg at 2 h; AZD7687 (mg/kg) at 0 h",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of Morentin Gutierrez 2019 (median and 95% PI)."
  )
```

```{r figure-3-compare}
fig3 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,      ~time, ~fig_median,
  "Vehicle",     5,         405,
  "Vehicle",     8,         375,
  "0.1",         5,         300,
  "0.3",         8,         220,
  "3",           8,         130,
  "Naive",       8,         105
)
cmp_r <- sim_r |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% c(5, 8)) |>
  group_by(arm, time) |>
  summarise(sim_median = median(tg), .groups = "drop") |>
  inner_join(fig3, by = c("arm", "time"))
stopifnot(nrow(cmp_r) == nrow(fig3))
cmp_r |>
  mutate(sim_median = round(sim_median, 0)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Rat plasma TAG (mg/dL): simulated median vs Figure 3 (read from the plot).")
# The vehicle and 0.1 mg/kg medians run 15-30% below Figure 3 (see
# Assumptions and deviations); the bound still fails a per-kg oil dose
# (+160%) or a mis-transcribed VTAG or kout.
stopifnot(all(abs(cmp_r$sim_median / cmp_r$fig_median - 1) < 0.45))
```

# Mass balance of the TAG excursion

The TAG equation is linear in the meal input, so without drug the incremental
area above baseline from one meal equals `Dose / (VTAG * kout)` exactly. Checked
on the typical values of each species (one challenge, long window).

```{r mass-balance}
mb_check <- function(mod, tg_mg, horizon, extra = list()) {
  ev <- bind_rows(
    tibble(time = 0, amt = tg_mg, cmt = "depot_tg", evid = 1),
    tibble(time = seq(0, horizon, by = 0.01), amt = 0, cmt = "tg", evid = 0)
  )
  for (nm in names(extra)) ev[[nm]] <- extra[[nm]]
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = ev, atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-10) |>
    as.data.frame()
  inc <- s$tg - s$rbase_tg[1]
  iauc <- sum(diff(s$time) * (head(inc, -1) + tail(inc, -1)) / 2)
  expected <- tg_mg / (s$vc_tg[1] * s$kout_tg[1])
  c(iAUC = iauc, expected = expected, rel_err = iauc / expected - 1)
}
mb <- rbind(
  human = mb_check(mod_h, meal_mg(0.60), 72, list(WT = 85.3, BMI = 27.5)),
  rat = mb_check(mod_r, rat_oil_mg, 120),
  mouse = mb_check(mod_m, mouse_oil_mg, 24)
)
knitr::kable(signif(mb, 4), caption = "Incremental TAG AUC (mg*h/dL): trapezoid vs Dose/(VTAG*kout).")
stopifnot(all(abs(mb[, "rel_err"]) < 0.005))

# A naive rat (no oil) stays at its baseline.
naive <- sim_r |> dplyr::filter(arm == "Naive") |> group_by(id) |>
  summarise(dev = max(abs(tg / rbase_tg - 1)), .groups = "drop")
stopifnot(max(naive$dev) < 1e-6)
```

# Cross-species potency

```{r potency}
data.frame(
  species = c("human", "rat", "mouse"),
  IC50_free_umolL = c(0.0078, 0.162, 0.081),
  IC50_free_ngmL = round(c(0.0078, 0.162, 0.081) * mw_azd7687, 2)
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "In vivo free IC50 of AZD7687 on meal TAG input (Table 1).")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Dose units.** The paper states concentrations and IC50 in umol/L but does
  not state the dose unit used in the fit. The models take AZD7687 in umol
  (human) or umol/kg (rodents), converting mg with the molecular weight 367.4
  g/mol (C21H25N3O3, PubChem CID 42636350; not printed in the paper). With this
  conversion the simulated free Cmax after 20 mg (~0.14 umol/L) matches
  Supplementary Figure 2B, which a mg-based dose would miss by a factor of
  ~370.
- **Rodent PK per kg, rodent TAG per animal.** The rodent CL and V are per kg
  (Supplementary Tables 2-3 give L/kg and L/(kg*hr); main-text Table 1 prints
  "L"), so the AZD7687 dose is per kg. The fat challenge goes into `depot_tg`
  as mg per animal, computed from the nominal ~230 g (rat) and ~25 g (mouse)
  body weights in Methods; this is the reading under which VTAG (dL) reproduces
  Figures 3 and 4 (a per-kg fat dose would put the mouse TAG peak above
  100,000 mg/dL).
- **Mouse fat amount.** "Intralipos 20%" was taken as 20% soybean oil by
  volume, converted with the 0.917 g/mL density the paper quotes.
- **IIV scale.** The paper reports IIV as a percentage; it was converted to a
  log-normal variance with `omega^2 = log(CV^2 + 1)`. For the 223% IIV on the
  human IC50, the readings `log(CV^2 + 1)` and `CV^2` give variances of 1.79 and
  4.99. With the first, the simulated human 97.5th percentiles lie within about
  20% of Figure 2's (table above).
- **Correlations.** Phoenix correlations (CL-V1 0.59 human, CL-V 0.419 mouse)
  were converted to covariances with the corresponding variances.
- **Combined residual error.** Phoenix "additive + multiplicative" PK error
  is encoded as nlmixr2's combined error (`add(addSd) + prop(propSd)`,
  variances summed).
- **Value discrepancies between the main text and the supplement.** Rat R0 is
  109.2 mg/dL in Table 1 and 109.3 mg/dL in Supplementary Table 5; the main-text
  value is used. Mouse R0 (178.07 vs 178.0) and mouse IC50 (0.081 vs 0.08) use
  the more precise of the two printings.
- **Rat TAG amplitude.** With the printed rat parameters the simulated
  vehicle-group median at 5-8 h (about 280 mg/dL) is about 30% below the
  Figure 3 median (about 375-405 mg/dL), and the simulated 97.5th percentile
  is well below the published upper bound (about 1000 mg/dL). The gap is
  in amplitude, not variability: the median is unchanged whether the reported
  IIV percentages are read as CVs, as standard deviations or as variances. The
  human and mouse fits, which share the structure and the unit conventions,
  match their figures to within about 15%. The cause could not be identified
  from the paper. Accounting for it through the oil amount would need rats of
  about 400 g, against the ~230 g in Methods. The printed parameters are kept
  unchanged.
- **Prediction intervals.** The simulated intervals are for the model
  prediction without residual error, so they are somewhat narrower than the
  published ones if Phoenix included residual error in its 1000 simulated data
  sets.
- **Virtual human cohort.** The paper gives only the mean body weight (85.3 kg)
  and mean BMI (27.5 kg/m^2); both were drawn log-normally around those means
  (CV about 14% and 12%). The Figure 2 replication uses 150 subjects per arm
  against the paper's 6-8 per cohort, so the simulated median and percentiles
  describe the model rather than the small observed cohorts.
- **Figure values.** The comparison values for Figures 2-4 were read from the
  published plots by the maintainers (approximately +/-10 mg/dL for Figure 2,
  +/-20 mg/dL for Figures 3-4).
- **`tg` and `depot_tg`** are not yet canonical compartment names; they are
  declared paper-specific, as in the other triglyceride models in the library.
- No erratum or correction notice for this article was found in Europe PMC
  (checked 2026-11-25).
